You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From f75c9f110f0bc2cba401a8b95c9c4377c6c057e9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eran Mizrahi <eranmizra@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2011 21:10:37 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

This fixes a problem introduced by commit 43e45eb94e1
which (wrongly) handled the 0xFEFF mark as RTL.

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766
---
 core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
index 88f72594567..54bb57f0a80 100644
--- a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
+++ b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
@@ -1692,7 +1692,7 @@ public class TextUtils {
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }
 
     /**
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by incorrect handling of the Unicode character 0xFEFF, which is a special marker known as the Zero Width No-Break Space (ZWNBSP) or Byte Order Mark (BOM). The previous implementation mistakenly treated this character as part of the range indicating right-to-left (RTL) text, leading to improper text direction handling. The patch corrects this by adjusting the range to exclude 0xFEFF, ensuring that it is not misclassified as RTL.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by incorrect handling of the Unicode character 0xFEFF, which is a special marker known as the Zero Width No-Break Space (ZWNBSP) or Byte Order Mark (BOM). The previous implementation mistakenly treated this character as part of the range indicating right-to-left (RTL) text, leading to improper text direction handling. The patch corrects this by adjusting the range to exclude 0xFEFF, ensuring that it is not misclassified as RTL.
